Overview of the race
- The Tour de Wallonie (Tour de la Région Wallonne) is a multi-day road cycling stage race held in the Wallonia region of Belgium.
- It is part of the UCI Europe Tour and historically has attracted a mix of WorldTour, ProTeam and Continental teams. In recent editions it has been a high-ranked stage race on the Europe Tour calendar.
- The race typically lasts five days and traverses varied terrain in Wallonia — rolling hills, short climbs, occasional punchy summit finishes and some flatter stages that suit sprinters. It is often used by riders preparing for late-summer targets or as a goal itself for riders from Belgium and neighboring countries.

2019 edition — summary

- The race included a mix of stage profiles: sprinter-friendly stages, rolling/hilly days, and at least one stage with more selective climbing that decided the general classification.
- The overall winner was a strong rider who performed well on the decisive stages and held time bonuses/lead across the race. The podium and classification winners included riders who performed consistently across the hilly stages and intermediate sprints.
